messages:
ryan: Heads-up — odd eviction cascade in ap-southeast2-rack17. Small GPU jobs getting preempted in waves; nodes show 95% alloc but lots of tiny pending pods. Cost hit if we keep reserving extra racks :frowning:
infra-bot: [alert] 8364123456 node/rg-rack17-node-03 eviction spike (count=18)
ryan: repro steps: deploy small batch of 0.25g pods (ai-worker:latest) across the namespace and watch scheduler pack then start soft-preempting.
ryan: kubectl get pods -n ai-team -o wide | grep Pending
```
ai-worker-5qz2   0/1 Pending   0   2m   <none>   rg-rack17-node-02   (<none>)
ai-worker-b9k1   0/1 Pending   0   1m   <none>   rg-rack17-node-03   (<none>)
```
ryan: nodes look full but with tiny fragment holes. suspect preferredDuringScheduling affinity + "gpu-reserved: true" taint interplay.
marta: ugh, this is the affinity + reserve-margin we added for reserved capacity. setting soft-affinity weights to 100 caused scheduler to stretch pods across racks?
samir: Can you paste a pod describe + node labels? Also post scheduler logs around mount time if you have them.
ryan: pod describe snippet:
```
Name: ai-worker-5qz2
Tolerations: key=gpu-reserved:NoSchedule
Affinity: preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
  - weight: 100
    podAffinityTerm: ... topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname
```
ryan: node labels on rg-rack17-node-03: `gpu.type=v100, rack=17, reserved=true, warmpool=true`
kai: quick theory: reserved=true nodes have a soft taint/annotation that reduces score for non-reserved pods, but preferredDuringScheduling with high weight + topology spread is causing the scheduler to place a few large pods then block many small ones — system falls back to preempting the small ones later because of the reserved policy. looks like packing is non-binpack-friendly.
marta: agreed. This is the cost tradeoff we feared: reserving racks for Dedicated customers but letting scheduler prefer them for regular pods if weights are high. Leads to fragmentation and eviction churn.
samir: proposed quick mitigations:
- reduce preferredDuringScheduling weight from 100 -> 20 for non-critical pools
- make reserved taint NoSchedule (hard) for reserved nodes and create explicit exception for dedicated workloads
- temporarily increase warm-pool size in ap-southeast2 to absorb tiny pods
- tune preemption policy to prefer evicting large non-guaranteed pods first (lower PDB impact)
ryan: testing change to weight=20 on staging now, will spam 200 tiny pods and watch.
ops-runbook-bot: runbook note: if eviction rate > 10/min escalate to infra-oncall and consider draining affected rack for investigation.
kai: long term we should add an allocation-decay heuristic in scheduler scoring: prefer contiguous binpack on GPUs by penalizing racks with >X fragmentation score. Also add metric `gpu_fragmentation_ratio` to the console.
marta: adding a short-term guard: update autoscaler to allocate extra tiny slots to a dedicated tiny-pool group rather than spreading across reserved racks. That should reduce cross-rack scatter.
samir: FYI cost impact estimate: extra 2 racks reserved to hit SLAs for a week -> ~$35k. If we reduce misplacements we probably recover $20k/week in reduced spill provisioning.
ryan: rolling weight change to prod in 5. Will report back in 15m.
ryan: (15m) weight change landed; initial pass looks better — pods are packing to warmpool nodes and evictions dropped from 18 -> 3 in rack17. still watching for ripple.
ryan: will open a follow-up with perf graphs + recommended policy patch. Thanks all :thumbsup:
